subject: data.frame error: Plotting layers that use different data sets

messages.author: 77a003add8c13e0a
messages.subject: data.frame error: Plotting layers that use different data sets
parts:
Hello all,

I'm trying to plot a fitted model line with uncertainty over my
original data points. I want a plot with 2 layers - 1st layer is the
observed values in qplot (habitat vs. abundance data, N=22) and the
2nd layer uses a new dataset of predicted model values to overlay the
predicted model fit with 95% confidence intervals using geom_ribbon.

The original plot is:
>h <- qplot (pc2, pmdens, data=data, xlab="Habitat PC2", ylab="Density")

From a zero-inflated model, I have calculated the model-predicted Y
values using a new 'dummy' dataset (MyData) from a sequence of the
range of x-values. I have also calculated the standard error + 95% CIs
of the model fit.

>MyData<-data.frame(pc2=seq(from=-3, to=3.1, by=0.01))
>Pred <- predict(model, newdata=MyData, type="response")
>upperY <- Pred + 1.96*seY
>lowerY <- Pred - 1.96*seY

I have then joined these predicted model fits into a new dataframe to
superimpose a geom_ribbon layer onto the original qplot

>preds <- data.frame("x"=MyData$pc2, "Pred"=Pred, "ymax"=upperY, "ymin"=lowerY)

I am now trying to add a geom_ribbon layer onto my qplot showing the
confidence intervals.

>h + geom_ribbon(aes(data=preds, x=preds$x, ymin=preds$ymin, ymax=preds$ymax))

...and get the error:
> h + geom_ribbon(aes(data=preds, x=preds$x, ymin=preds$ymin, ymax=preds$ymax))
Error in data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE) :
arguments imply differing number of rows: 611, 22

The original 'data' data.frame has N=22 rows and the 'preds'
data.frame has N=611 rows. I know ggplot2 is smart enough to deal with
different datasets on different layers, so what have I done wrong?
Maybe something in specifying the new 'preds' data.frame?

Thank you very much, Emily

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: data.frame error: Plotting layers that use different data sets
parts:
Hi Emily,

You've got the syntax confused a little. You want:

h + geom_ribbon(data=preds, aes(x = x, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax))

Hadley
